column3: Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has “spirits” and makes the LORD the active weigher; BSB has motives being weighed.
Hebrew says “roll” the works and that the plans are “established”; BSB has “commit” and “achieved.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew retains the idiom “hand to hand”; BSB interprets it as “be assured.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “without justice”; BSB has “with injustice.”
Hebrew has singular “his step”; BSB has plural steps.
Hebrew has a direct negative statement about the king’s mouth; BSB makes it an obligation with “must not.”
Hebrew calls the weights His “work,” rather than His “concern,” and explicitly names weight-stones.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew has plural kings in the first clause and an active “he loves” in the second; BSB has a singular king and passive “is beloved.”
Hebrew has plural “messengers of death”; BSB has a singular messenger.
Hebrew names the late rain; BSB interprets it as spring rain.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew says “his soul”; BSB has “his life.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew can name a matter or word; BSB specifies instruction and renders the good found as success.
Hebrew uses the image “sweetness of lips”; BSB has “pleasant speech.”
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew repeats the word for instruction used in verse 21; BSB renders it here “persuasiveness.”
Hebrew has singular “bone”; BSB has plural bones.
Hebrew ends with plural “ways of death”; BSB has a singular way.
Hebrew expressly names the soul and mouth; BSB interprets these as appetite and hunger.
Hebrew places the fire image on “his lip”; BSB uses the broader “his speech.”
Hebrew has a singular close companion; BSB has plural close friends.
Close to the Hebrew.
Hebrew describes closing the eyes and completed evil; BSB has winking an eye and being bent on evil.
